Here we are looking at the 320 subject (24 removed from VIF above 4)

```{r load data, include=FALSE}
load(here("data", "Cleaned_Pilot", "exclusions.2020.10.21.RData"))
#Neuroethics_Judgement <- readr::read_csv(here::here("data", "Cleaned_Pilot", "clean_data_long.csv"))
# Disable scientific notation
options(scipen=999)

Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
   dplyr::select("user_id", "condition", "Risk_Beta", "Gain_Beta", "vif.risk", "vif.gain", "marginal.effect.risk", "marginal.effect.gain", "No", "Yes", 
"Extraversion", "Agreeableness", "Conscientiousness", "Neuroticism", 
"Openness", "Harm", "Fairness", "Loyalty", "Athority", "Sancticy", 
"PerspectiveTaking", "Fantasy", "EmpathicConcern", "PersonalDistress", 
"POWER", "SELF.DIRECTION", "ACHIEVEMENT", "HEDONISM", "STIMULATION", 
"UNIVERSALISM", "BENEVOLENCE", "TRADITION", "CONFORMITY", "SECURITY", 
"Lying", "Assasination", "Torture", "Murder", "Stealing", "ForcedSterilization", 
"consequentialism.score", "moral.commitment", "SNS.total", "SNS.ability", 
"SNS.preference", "Berlin1", "Berlin2", "Berlin3", "Berlin4", 
"BerlinScore", "GRiPs_Score", "republican", "democrat", "independent", 
"conservative", "liberal", "conservatismFactor", "sex", "age", 
"race_ethnicity", "education", "ReligionRaised", "ReligionNow", 
"Religiosity", "Spirituality", "AttendChurch", "ReligiousActivity", 
"meditation", "RelationshipStatus", "Income", "YearOfEducation", "Political_Party", "Optimize"
) %>% 
   mutate(lambda = -Risk_Beta/Gain_Beta) %>%
   mutate(Risk_odds = exp(Risk_Beta)) %>%
   mutate(Gain_odds = exp(Gain_Beta)) %>%
   mutate(dominate = ifelse(Yes >= 75 *.80 | No >= 75 *.90, "dominate", "not_dominate")) %>% 
   filter(!dominate == "dominate") %>% 
   distinct() -> data.h
```

Individual differences

**In the R01 aims, I'm predicting that "more affluent, educated, liberal, and younger individuals will be less risk-averse and more benefit-driven." Is this true in our data?**

**Are more affluent less risk-averse and more benefit-driven?**

```{r income, echo=FALSE}
data.h %>% 
  dplyr::select(marginal.effect.risk, marginal.effect.gain, Income, Yes, No) -> data.income
data.income$Incomecat<-cut(data.h$Income, c(0, 25000,50000,75000, 200000))
data.income %>% 
  mutate(income_recode = fct_recode(Incomecat,
  "< 25,000" = "(0,2.5e+04]",
  "25,000-50,000" = "(2.5e+04,5e+04]",
  "50,000-75,000"= "(5e+04,7.5e+04]",
  "> 75,000" = "(7.5e+04,2e+05]")) %>% 
  filter(!Income == 0) %>% 
  mutate(Income = log(Income))-> data.income
 
#risk 
lm.income.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~ Income, data.income)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.income.risk), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")], caption = "Predicting Risk given Continuous Income")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

lm.income.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~ income_recode, data.income)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.income.risk), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")], caption = "Predicting Risk given Categorical Income")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

ggplot(data.income, aes(x=log(Income), y=marginal.effect.risk)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "red") +
    geom_point()

income <- data.income %>% 
  group_by(income_recode) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
         mean = mean(marginal.effect.risk),
         sd = sd(marginal.effect.risk),
         se = sd / sqrt(n),
         ci = qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n)) %>% na.omit()
knitr::kable(income, caption = "Descriptives for risk by income")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
# plot the means and standard errors
ggplot(income, 
       aes(x = income_recode, 
           y = mean, 
           group = 1)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, 
                    ymax = mean + se), 
                width = .1) + 
   labs(x = "Income", 
       y = "Mean", 
       title  = "Risk by Income")

#gain 
lm.income.gain <- lm(marginal.effect.gain ~Income, data.income)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.income.gain), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")], caption = "Predicting Gain given Continuous Income")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

lm.income.gain <- lm(marginal.effect.gain ~ income_recode, data.income)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.income.gain), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")], caption = "Predicting Gain given Categorical Income")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

ggplot(data.income, aes(x=log(Income), y=marginal.effect.gain)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "red") +
    geom_point()

income <- data.income %>% 
  group_by(income_recode) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
         mean = mean(marginal.effect.gain),
         sd = sd(marginal.effect.gain),
         se = sd / sqrt(n),
         ci = qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n)) %>% na.omit()
knitr::kable(income, caption = "Descriptives for gain by income")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
# plot the means and standard errors
ggplot(income, 
       aes(x = income_recode, 
           y = mean, 
           group = 1)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, 
                    ymax = mean + se), 
                width = .1)+
  labs(x = "Income", 
       y = "Mean", 
       title  = "Gain by Income")


```

*We did not find differences across Income for Risk or Gain in our sample*



**Are more educated less risk-averse and more benefit-driven?**

```{r education, echo=FALSE}
data.h %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id, marginal.effect.risk, marginal.effect.gain, education, Yes, No) -> data.education
data.education %>% 
  filter(!user_id == "RU3gTWzp") %>% #we only have a single subject with less than a high school degee
  mutate(education_recode = fct_recode(education,
  HighSchool = "high school degree",
  Undergraduate = "bachelor",
  Postgraduate = "masters",
  Postgraduate = "Doctoral/Professional"
))  -> data.education #then we sum code for the models 

#risk 
lm.education.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~education_recode, data.education)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.education.risk), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")], caption = "Predicting Risk given Categorical Education")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

education <- data.education %>%
  group_by(education_recode) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
         mean = mean(marginal.effect.risk),
         sd = sd(marginal.effect.risk),
         se = sd / sqrt(n),
         ci = qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n))
knitr::kable(education, caption = "Descriptives for risk by education")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
# plot the means and standard errors
ggplot(education, 
       aes(x = education_recode, 
           y = mean, 
           group = 1)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, 
                    ymax = mean + se), 
                width = .1)+
    labs(x = "Education", 
       y = "Mean", 
       title  = "Risk by Education")

# creating a basic plot
p <- ggplot(data.education, aes(education_recode, marginal.effect.risk, fill = education_recode)) +
  geom_boxplot()

# using `pairwiseComparisons` package to create a dataframe with results
df <-
  pairwise_comparisons(data.education, education_recode, marginal.effect.risk, messages = FALSE, var.equal = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(.data = ., groups = purrr::pmap(.l = list(group1, group2), .f = c)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(.data = ., group1)
knitr::kable(df[c("group1", "group2", "p.value", "significance", "test.details")],caption = "Pairwise comparisons for risk by education")%>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

p +
  ggsignif::geom_signif(
    comparisons = df$groups,
    map_signif_level = TRUE,
    tip_length = 0.01,
    y_position = c(-0.01, .02, .001),
    annotations = df$label,
    test = NULL,
    na.rm = TRUE,
    parse = TRUE
  )

#gain
lm.education.gain <- lm(marginal.effect.gain ~education, data.education)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.education.gain), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")], caption = "Predicting Gain given Categorical Education")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

education <- data.education %>%
  group_by(education_recode) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
         mean = mean(marginal.effect.gain),
         sd = sd(marginal.effect.gain),
         se = sd / sqrt(n),
         ci = qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sd / sqrt(n))
knitr::kable(education, caption = "Descriptives for gain by education")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
# plot the means and standard errors
ggplot(education, 
       aes(x = education_recode, 
           y = mean, 
           group = 1)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, 
                    ymax = mean + se), 
                width = .1) +
   labs(x = "Education", 
       y = "Mean", 
       title  = "Gain by Education")

# creating a basic plot
p <- ggplot(data.education, aes(education_recode, marginal.effect.gain, fill = education_recode)) +
  geom_boxplot()

# using `pairwiseComparisons` package to create a dataframe with results
df <-
  pairwise_comparisons(data.education, education_recode, marginal.effect.gain, messages = FALSE, var.equal = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(.data = ., groups = purrr::pmap(.l = list(group1, group2), .f = c)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(.data = ., group1)
knitr::kable(df[c("group1", "group2", "p.value", "significance", "test.details")],caption = "Pairwise comparisons for gain by education")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")


p +
  ggsignif::geom_signif(
    comparisons = df$groups,
    map_signif_level = TRUE,
    tip_length = 0.01,
    y_position = c(-0.01, .02, .001),
    annotations = df$label,
    test = NULL,
    na.rm = TRUE,
    parse = TRUE
  )

###both in one graph
data.education %>% 
  dplyr::select(education_recode, marginal.effect.risk, marginal.effect.gain) %>% 
  mutate(marginal.effect.risk = -marginal.effect.risk) %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id = "education_recode" , variable.name = "type", value.name = "beta") -> plotdata

education <- plotdata %>%
  group_by(education_recode, type) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
            mean = mean(beta),
            sd = sd(beta),
            se = sd/sqrt(n))

pd <- position_dodge(0.2)
ggplot(education, 
       aes(x = factor(education_recode, 
                      labels = c("High School",
                                 "Undergraduate",
                                 "Postgraduate")), 
           y = mean, 
           group=type, 
           color=type)) +
  geom_point(position=pd, 
             size = 3) +
  geom_line(position = pd, 
            size = 1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, 
                    ymax = mean + se), 
                width = .1, 
                position = pd, 
                size = 1) +
  #scale_y_continuous(label = scales::dollar) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette="Set1") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Mean AME by type and eduation",
       subtitle = "(mean +/- standard error)",
       x = "", 
       y = "",
       color = "Attribute")


data.education %>% 
  dplyr::select(education_recode, marginal.effect.risk, marginal.effect.gain, Yes, No) %>% 
  mutate(marginal.effect.risk = -marginal.effect.risk) %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id = c("education_recode", "Yes", "No") , variable.name = "type", value.name = "beta") -> test

lm.education <- lm(beta~ type*education_recode*No, test)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.education), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")], caption = "Predicting AME given R/B and education")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
```

Brown, S., Ortiz, A., & Taylor, K. (2006). Educational Attainment and Risk Preference. 31.

*We found a difference between high school and post grads for both risk and gain.*

**Are younger individuals less risk-averse and more benefit-driven?**

```{r age, echo=FALSE}
data.h %>% 
  dplyr::select(marginal.effect.risk, marginal.effect.gain, age, Yes, No) -> data.age
data.age$Agecat   <-cut(data.age$age, c(18,24,49,75))
data.age %>% 
   mutate(age_recode = fct_recode(Agecat,
  "18-24" = "(18,24]",
  "25-49" = "(24,49]",
  "50-75" = "(49,75]")) -> data.age

data.age$age_recode <- relevel(data.age$age_recode, "18-24")

#risk 
lm.age.risk <- lm(marginal.effect.risk ~ poly(age,2), data.age)
```

```{r multivariate, echo=FALSE}

data.multivariate <- data_frame(
  user_id = data.h$user_id,
  risk = data.h$marginal.effect.risk,
  gain = data.h$marginal.effect.gain,
  religion = data.religious$Religiosity,
  age = data.age$age,
  political = data.political$conservatismFactor,
  income = data.income$Income,
  education = data.h$education,
  sex = data.h$sex
  ) %>% 
  filter(!user_id == "RU3gTWzp") %>% #we only have a single subject with less than a high school degee
  mutate(education = fct_recode(education,
  HighSchool = "high school degree",
  Undergraduate = "bachelor",
  Postgraduate = "masters",
  Postgraduate = "Doctoral/Professional"
  )) %>% 
  filter(!sex == "Other") %>% 
  mutate(race_ethnicity = fct_recode(race_ethnicity,
  Black = "Black",
  White = "White",
  Hispanic = "Hispanic or Latino",
  Asian = "Asian",
  Other = "Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander",
  Other = "American Indian/Alaska Native",
  Other = "Mixed",
  Other = "Other",
  No = "Prefer not to say"
  )) %>% 
  filter(!user_id == "5pd8VS5F") 

lm.multi.risk <- lm(risk ~ religion + age  + political + income + education + race_ethnicity + sex, data.multivariate)

lm.multi.gain <- lm(risk ~ religion + age  + political + income + education + race_ethnicity + sex, data.multivariate)

tab <- map_df(list(lm.multi.risk), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "statistic", "p.value")], caption = "Predicting risk given mutltivariate")%>%
```

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(semPlot)
library(lavaan)
model <- '
  marginal.effect.risk  =~ religion + age  + political + income + education + race_ethnicity + sex
  marginal.effect.gain  =~ religion + age  + political + income + education + race_ethnicity + sex
  
  marginal.effect.gain ~~ marginal.effect.risk'

test <- data.matrix(data.multivariate)

test <- data.matrix(data.multivariate[,c("education",  "race_ethnicity",  "sex")])

model.fit <- lavaan::cfa(model, test)

semPaths(model.fit, what = "std", edge.label.cex = 0.7,
         edge.color = 1, esize =1 , sizeMan = 4.5, asize = 2.5, 
         intercepts = F, rotation = 4, thresholdColor = "red",
         mar = c(1,5,1.5,5), fade =F, nCharNodes = 4)

fitmeasures(model.fit) ##fit indices

summary(model.fit,
        standardized=TRUE,
        rsquare = TRUE)
parameterestimates(model.fit, standardized=TRUE) ##CIs for parameters
fitted(model.fit) ##look at cov table
residuals(model.fit) ##look at residuals
modificationindices(model.fit, sort. = T) ##modification indices


```

```{r multi level individual differences test}
Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
  mutate(dominate = ifelse(Yes >= 75 *.80 | No >= 75 *.90, "dominate", "not_dominate")) %>% 
  filter(!dominate == "dominate") %>% 
  filter(!user_id == "RU3gTWzp")  -> data
###### MER for each subject
m.marginal <- by(data, data$user_id, function(x) margins::margins(glm(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk  + gain, data = x, family = binomial(link = "logit"))))

#run logit model
user_id <- names(m.marginal)
marginal.effect <- list()
n=377
for (i in 1:n){
dat = m.marginal[[i]]
  marginal.effect[[i]] = dat
}
subjectModels.marginal <- do.call(rbind, marginal.effect)
subjectModels.marginal %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id, risk,gain,dydx_risk, dydx_gain) -> test
test <- merge(data.h, test, "user_id")

library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
lm.base <- lmer(dydx_risk ~ 1 + (1 | user_id) + (1 | user_id:condition),
                data = test, REML = F, lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
lm.1 <- lmer(dydx_risk ~ 1 + Fairness +(1 | user_id),
                data = test, REML = F, lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
lm.2 <- lmer(dydx_risk ~ education + (1 | user_id) + (1 | user_id:condition),
                data = test, REML = F, lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
summary(lm.2)
```
